meta.title: Amara — an AI tutor that works without internet
meta.description: Amara is a working prototype of an AI tutor that runs entirely on a laptop: no Wi-Fi, no cloud, and no student data leaving the room. Built on Tether's QVAC.
meta.ogDescription: A working prototype that runs entirely on a laptop. No Wi-Fi, no cloud, no data leaving the room.

hero.title: A tutor for schools the internet hasn't reached.
hero.lede: Amara is an AI tutor that runs entirely on a laptop. No Wi-Fi, no cloud, and no student data leaving the room.
hero.free: A non-profit project. The app is completely free.

thesis.library: A library waits for a child to know what to look for and to understand what they find.
thesis.amara: Amara starts from what the child doesn't understand.

film.title: The tutor in the film is real.
film.intro: The film is illustrated. Halfway through, it cuts to a screen recording of the working prototype answering a student's question on a laptop.

facts.speed: until the first words of an answer appear, with the model running on the laptop itself.
facts.speedNote: Measured on a MacBook Pro with M1 Pro and 16 GB of memory.
facts.network: network connections while it answers. Every route out is blocked and monitored during the tests.
facts.cited: Every answer shows the article it came from. When its materials don't cover a question, it says "I don't know" instead of guessing.
facts.citedNote: Sources are attached by the app, not written by the model.

how.title: What happens when a student asks a question
how.imageAlt: Illustration: Amara opens an old laptop on her school desk while two classmates lean in.
how.step1Text: A filter screens it first, so off-topic or unsafe questions get a gentle redirect.
how.step2: The laptop searches its own library
how.step2Text: A pack of openly licensed science and maths articles is stored on the device and searched locally.
how.step3: A small model writes the explanation
how.step3Text: Qwen3 4B runs on the laptop through Tether's QVAC and explains step by step, in simple words.
how.step4: The student gets a source and a question back
how.step4Text: The answer shows where it came from and ends with a question to check understanding.

limits.title: What it isn't yet
limits.lead: Amara is a working prototype. It has not been tested in a school, and these are the limits we know about.
limits.language: It answers in Spanish and English only.
limits.grading: It can't tell a student whether their answer is right. It thanks them and shows how to check.
limits.safety: Its safety filters look for words and can be worked around, so children should use it with an adult nearby.
limits.size: It's a small model on a laptop: far less capable than cloud assistants, and only as broad as its library.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.description: How Amara handles the details sent through the pilot request form.
privacy.intro: This page explains what happens to the details you send through the "Request a pilot" form. Amara is an independent prototype run by Alex Smith, who is responsible for these details.
privacy.collect: The name of your school or organization, country, your name and role, your email, the approximate number of students, connectivity, available devices, language of instruction, and your message if you write one. The form never asks for information about students, so please don't include any.
privacy.use: Only to reply to your request. It isn't used for marketing and isn't added to any mailing list.
privacy.whereTitle: Where it goes and for how long
privacy.whereResend: Resend delivers the form to me by email and keeps a copy for up to 30 days.
privacy.whereInbox: The email arrives in my Gmail inbox, where I keep it for up to 12 months.
privacy.whereVercel: Vercel hosts this site and may process technical data, such as your IP address, to serve the pages.
privacy.no: It uses no cookies, no analytics and no advertising, and I don't sell or share your details with anyone else.
privacy.tutor: This page is about the website. The tutor runs on the laptop, and the questions students ask it aren't sent anywhere.
privacy.rights: You can ask me to show, correct or delete your details at any time. Just write to me through the form or on
privacy.collectFeedback: The feedback form asks for your message and the type of message. Your computer or phone and your email are optional. It is used only to read your message, improve Amara and reply if you asked.
